context_requirements: Active cell cycle progression with dynamic microtubule polymerization
Tubulin heterodimer availability and microtubule assembly
Proliferating cells are more sensitive than quiescent/non-dividing cells
Intact mitotic checkpoint machinery to translate microtubule disruption into G2/M arrest
falsifiers: No enrichment of G2/M arrest or mitotic proliferation-down signature at 24 h in responsive lines
No induction of CDKN1A, GADD45A, or apoptosis markers at 24 h despite antiproliferative concentrations
Strong transcriptional response in non-proliferating HA1E cells comparable to cancer lines
Lack of any dose- or time-dependent change in cell-cycle genes across all nine lines

evidence.supports: Tubulin polymerization inhibitors induce G2/M cell cycle arrest and apoptosis in cancer cells
Tubulin polymerization inhibition is the mechanism of antiproliferative activity in multiple cancer cell lines
Tubulin inhibitors inhibit microtubule formation and induce G2/M arrest
Microtubule polymerization inhibition blocks cell cycle at G2-M and activates caspase-3/PARP apoptosis
Tubulin inhibitors bind the colchicine site and selectively inhibit proliferating cancer cells over quiescent lymphocytes

changes: Removed TUBB6 from proximal_down: tubulin polymerization inhibitors do not transcriptionally repress TUBB6 at 6 h; TUBB6 is not a validated immediate target of the mechanism.

Removed PLK1 and CCNB1 from late_up: these are mitotic genes typically induced or maintained during G2/M arrest, not consistently upregulated at 24 h; placing them in late_up contradicts the expected proliferation-down signature.
Removed CCNB1 from late_up to avoid conflict with late_down mitotic genes and because the cited abstracts do not support CCNB1 upregulation at 24 h.
Removed PLK1 from late_up because PLK1 is a mitotic kinase whose expression is not supported as upregulated by tubulin inhibition at 24 h in the cited evidence.
